questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It has been my dream for 5 years to go to Colombia, because I wanted to improve my spanish, and for me Colombia represents a country full of diversity (cultural, landscapes, nature, ethnic), and I think that is very beautiful

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: More or less, some things were a bit confusing, but everything got sorted out, and I think it's part of the experience that things are a bit confusing to begin with.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately I missed the introduction week because of exams, and during that week the other students got a lot of information and met each other. So I really recommend to go to the introduction week if you can.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was relly stressed about housing before going there, but actually it's not that difficult to find something. So don't worry.  If you want to life with others, I would not recommend to live at City U, the apartment is very small and it's not that nice. Then I would rather recommend living at LivinnX, it's also student accomodations but much nicer apartments. Otherwise there are also good oppourtunities to find apartment and live  with other. But it's much nicer to live next to the campus so you can walk.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Read description above. I lived in something called the Spot, where you have your own small apartment which was nice, but I regret I didn't chose LivingX.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a messy and very confusing to understand how it works. I found it frustrating. And then I ended up with almost all the courses I wanted to, which was nice, but the process was annoying. So just be prepare for that, but don't worry as it will be sorted out. For example my llast course got approved the week the courses started.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Yes you could easily ask the persons in charge of the mobility program.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 2 out of 3 courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can sign up for more credits than you need, so do that, because it's nice to try the course and afterwards drop it. And sign up for sports clases- salsa bachata beginner is awesome!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: You have to attend classes and there is quite a lot of work during the semester, assignments, test, stuff like that. I wouldn't say it's super difficult, I think the level some times may be a bit lower than UCPH (depends on the course).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot of the master courses are hibrid but more online. It was a bit disapointing and not very motivating. Furthermore there are either in the morning like 7-9 or afternoon 15-19 because the colombians that are enrolled in their master are working full time.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Género e interdisciplinariedad
- Teorías de desarollo
- Teorías de relaciones internationales

Ekstra credit
- Espanol lengua extranjera
- Salsa bachata

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I wouldn't recommend the courses I had.

What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many sports clases but also creative classes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I already said bachata salsa haha
And if I could do it again, I would have chosen an art course.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is a loooooot. I can't list everything here, you'll figure it out ;)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, colombians are really nice

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do sports classes and other activites.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing, I have also travelled in south america before.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everything I love Colombia. The culture, the people, the street food, the landscape, the openness, the salsa culture in bars.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Even though the course registration is annoying, don't worry you'll be fine
2. Be open to all the different exchange students, don't stay in a european bobble, take initiative, organize a barbecue or something
3. Don't worry about housing, some of my friends even change accomodations during the stay, there are many places available.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry if your spanish isn't perfect, mine is neither, and you don't need perfect spanish to pass the courses. Take extra spanish class at the university.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was a challenge with the online classes and not being there at the introduction week. I feel like I missed out on some relations.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
